title: The pro-étale direct image for objects of étale origin
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum: a prime $p$, a prime power $q=p^r$ with $r\geq1$, a field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Set $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$, the finite coefficient ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $d\in\mathbf N$, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose $\dim X\leq d$ for topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $f:X	o Y$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type. Let $a\leq b$ be integers and let $K'\in D(X_{\Et},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] be bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Here $X_{\Et}$ denotes the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\Et}$ for $T=X,Y$ denote the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with its derived pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] admit a derived isomorphism $K\cong
u_X^*K'$. Then the ordinary pro-étale derived direct image $Rf_*K$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] is bounded constructible on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. In particular it belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: Finite type includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The assumed separatedness gives quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Thus $f$ has both geometric hypotheses of the comparison theorem; $K'$ is bounded below because it is bounded.

Put $L=Rf_{\Et,*}K'$. Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper] to $K'$: the coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$, finite-type $k$-schemes, separated finite-type $f$, source bound $\dim X\le d$, bounded constructibility and input Tor interval are precisely its hypotheses. It gives that $L$ is bounded constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ with Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$. In particular $L\in D^+(Y_{\Et},A)$. The private equivalence boundedConstructible_iff converts between the two recorded finite-ring constructibility predicates using [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison]; their boundedness conditions are equivalent by the cohomological t-structure characterization.

source.place: second paragraph, application of étale direct-image corollary

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to the bounded-below object K' on the fixed-coefficient sites. Use [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility] and the exact comparison inclusion compatibility to express the resulting isomorphism for the ordinary unbounded right derived functors. Factor the intrinsic comparison as the exact fixed-scalar comparison followed by canonical coefficient realization. The section-normalized derived realization comparison of [def-sp-finite-intrinsic-direct-adjunction] identifies realization of the fixed-scalar direct image with the actual intrinsic constant-ring direct image. Compose with the direct image of the inverse of the supplied origin isomorphism to obtain e: nu_Y^* L ≅ Rf_* K. The witness (L,e) is the first conclusion, the etale-origin condition of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Every comparison is between the specified functors; there is no choice of a new direct image.

source.place: first paragraph, displayed derived comparison; second paragraph, bounded constructibility

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] to L in D+ and the ordered interval [a,b+2d]; the order follows from a ≤ b and d ≥ 0. Its output is the intrinsic realization of the bounded-below comparison image. Exact derived inclusion compatibility and composition give an isomorphism from this object to the intrinsic comparison of L, then e identifies it with Rf_*K. For the resolution-based predicate [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], transport is immediate without choosing tensors: a representative isomorphism Q(M) ≅ Rf_*K composed with the inverse comparison isomorphism is a representative isomorphism to the source. The original universal K-flat resolution test then gives exactly the same vanishing assertion. This proves the second conclusion with every intrinsic module sheaf as test object, using [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

source.place: second paragraph, transfer of the Tor interval and conclusion

proof.text: For the intrinsic bounded constructibility of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], let F be intrinsic comparison. The exact derived homology comparison [def-sfb-exact-derived-cohomology-comparison], followed by H^i(e), gives F(H^i L) ≅ H^i(Rf_*K). The finite interval [c,g] bounding the nonzero cohomology of L bounds the latter cohomology as well, since F preserves zero objects; hence its support is a subset of the finite integer interval [c,g]. For constructibility, use [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] to read H^i L as a constructible sheaf in the source-library convention. The proved source theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isConstructible_comparisonUpperStar_obj preserves that condition. The canonical restriction isomorphism [lem-sf-intrinsic-realization-origin-comparison] identifies its intrinsic realization after restriction to constant scalars with this fixed-coefficient image. Compose with the restricted homology isomorphism, transport fixed-coefficient constructibility along that isomorphism, and apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-constructibility] to obtain intrinsic constructibility of H^i(Rf_*K). This directly proves the needed forward preservation statement, without the full constructible-origin equivalence. Together with the interval from step 4, the definition [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] gives the final conclusion. The prime inequality is used by the etale direct-image corollary; no additional invertibility hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: second paragraph, last sentence: the corollary is clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary; the reading of bounded constructible pro-étale objects as étale-origin objects (clause (3) of lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative in the blueprint) is supplied by lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin (ii)

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper], let
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be of étale origin: $K\cong\nu_X^*K'$
for the comparison morphism
of sites and a bounded constructible complex $K'$ of $A$-modules on
$X_{\Et}$ of finite Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$. Then the pro-étale direct image $Rf_*K$ is bounded
constructible on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b+2d]$; that is, clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary holds at
the finite coefficient ring $A$ for such $K$.

proof.text:
The morphism $f$ is of finite type, hence quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, so the comparison direct image of
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives an isomorphism

$$
\nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}K'\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}\nu_X^*K'
\cong Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}K .
$$

By [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper] the complex
$Rf_{\Et,*}K'$ is bounded constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ with finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$, and [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval]
transfers that Tor amplitude to its pullback
$\nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}K'$, which is the finite-Tor condition of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on the pro-étale site; bounded
constructibility of that pullback is
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible]. The
identification therefore exhibits $Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}K$ as a bounded
constructible pro-étale object of finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$.
By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] the bounded constructible
pro-étale objects are the pullbacks of the bounded constructible étale
objects, a reading recorded in clause (3) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative]; for those objects the
corollary is exactly clause (iii) of the finite-Tor preservation summary at the
finite coefficient ring $A$.

old_proof.text: Apply the forward implication of [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] with $T=Y$, the finite commutative ring $A$, the object $L\in D^+(Y_{\Et},A)$ of step 2 and the interval $[a,b+2d]$. If $a\le b$ then $a\le b+2d$ since $d\ge0$; if $a>b$, testing [def-kun-tor-amplitude] with $\mathcal M=A_X$ gives $\mathcal H^i(K')=0$ for all $i$, so $K'\cong0$, $L\cong0$ and $Rf_*K\cong0$, for which every vanishing below is immediate. The lemma gives Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$ for $\nu_Y^*L$ against every pro-étale module sheaf. For each such $M$, functoriality of derived tensor sends $e$ to an isomorphism $(\nu_Y^*L)\otimes_A^L M\cong (Rf_*K)\otimes_A^L M$; its cohomology isomorphisms identify the vanishing outside $[a,b+2d]$. old_proof.text:
Membership in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. The category $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] is defined inside $D^b_c(Y,A)$ of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the intrinsic bounded constructible category (finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, each constructible for a finite partition into locally closed constructible subschemes), not inside the étale-origin category $\Dbc(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ of step 3; the two are not identified by definition. Apply clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] with $T=Y$ and $A=A_{E,n}$ to the object $L\in\Dbc(Y_{\Et},A)$ of step 2: $
u_Y^*L$ has finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, all intrinsically constructible. Since $e$ induces isomorphisms $\mathcal H^q(
u_Y^*L)\cong\mathcal H^q(Rf_*K)$ and constructibility of a sheaf is invariant under isomorphism, $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on $Y$, a $k$-scheme with $\ell
eq p$, as [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] requires. With step 4, $Rf_*K$ is an object of $D^b_c(Y,A)$ with Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$, i.e. $Rf_*K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, which proves the final clause.
